flags: Homeowners of America Holding Corporation and Porch Insurance Reciprocal Exchange entered into a definitive Purchase Agreement to acquire Allied Trust Insurance Company, Allied Underwriters LLC, and Lonestar Lagniappe Reinsurance Holdings, LLC, with up to $20.0 million at closing and up to $50.0 million in deferred payments optionally payable in Porch common stock.

Porch and the Reciprocal entered into an at-the-market Distribution Agreement with StoneX Financial Inc. under which the Reciprocal may sell up to 10 million existing shares and Porch may issue and sell up to 5 million shares at a 1.5% sales commission, pursuant to a registration statement filed the same day.

Porch formed Porch Reciprocal Exchange and sold its legacy homeowners insurance carrier, Homeowners of America, to the Reciprocal for approximately $105 million less $58 million of prior surplus note obligations, financed by a surplus note bringing total surplus notes held by Porch to approximately $106 million, alongside the transfer of 18.3 million Porch shares.

business_model.claim: Porch Group, Inc. operates four reportable segments: Insurance Services, Software & Data, and Consumer Services (owned by Porch), plus the Reciprocal Segment (managed, not owned, by Porch).
quotes: We operate under four reportable segments that are also our operating segments.
Three of these segments are owned by Porch — Insurance Services, Software & Data, and Consumer Services.

The fourth segment, the Reciprocal Segment, is managed, but not owned, by Porch and, at this time, is consolidated for reporting purposes as described in the basis of presentation section in Note 1 of the unaudited Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements.

business_model.claim: In January 2025, Porch formed Porch Reciprocal Exchange, sold its legacy carrier Homeowners of America to the Reciprocal, and shifted to managing the policyholder-owned exchange while consolidating it as a variable interest entity.
quotes: In January 2025, we completed the formation of the Reciprocal.
Following the sale, HOA became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reciprocal.
The Reciprocal is a separate legal entity, owned by its member policyholders, and is not owned, wholly or in part, by the Company.
The Reciprocal is consolidated in our financial statements solely as a result of the Company's variable interest in, and status as primary beneficiary of, the entity.

business_model.claim: The Insurance Services segment earns revenue by managing and operating the Reciprocal for commissions and fees, collecting policy fees from policyholders and lead fees from agencies, holding $106 million of Reciprocal surplus notes paying 9.75% plus SOFR interest, and providing captive reinsurance.
quotes: Our Insurance Services segment manages and operates the Reciprocal, providing services related, but not limited, to underwriting, policy renewal, risk management, insurance portfolio management, financial management, and setting investment guidelines in exchange for commissions and fees.

The Insurance Services segment also holds the surplus notes issued by the Reciprocal and includes our captive reinsurer which provides reinsurance support to improve capital efficiency for the Reciprocal.
In exchange for these services, Porch receives policy fees from policyholders and ongoing commissions from the Reciprocal.
Porch now holds $106 million of surplus notes due from the Reciprocal which pay interest of 9.75% plus SOFR.

business_model.claim: The Software & Data segment sells subscription and predominantly transactional software to inspection, mortgage, title, and roofing companies, and sells Home Factors property insights and mover marketing data products to insurance carriers and other businesses.
quotes: Our Software & Data segment provides, on a subscription and predominantly transactional basis, software to inspection, mortgage, title, and roofing companies and data products to insurance and other types of companies.

With insights into approximately 90% of U.S. homes, Home Factors provides interior and exterior attributes and condition data to help insurance carriers improve underwriting, pricing, and risk selection.

business_model.claim: The Consumer Services segment sells home warranty products across 50 states and Washington, D.C., and provides moving-related services such as movers, TV/Internet, and security to consumers.
quotes: Our warranty business offers various products such as whole-home, service line, and extended labor warranties in 50 states and Washington, D.C.
Our Consumer Services segment also provides moving-related services such as movers, TV/Internet, and security.

business_model.claim: The Reciprocal Segment sells property-related insurance products to consumers in 20 states through Homeowners of America and Porch Reciprocal Exchange, generating revenue primarily from policy premiums.
quotes: The Reciprocal Segment provides consumers with insurance to protect their homes, earning revenue primarily through premiums collected on policies.
The Reciprocal offers property-related insurance products in 20 states.

business_model.claim: Insurance Services revenue is driven by Reciprocal premium and policy volume, with Q3 2026 Reciprocal Written Premium reaching $161.0 million and Reciprocal Policies Written growing 42% year-over-year alongside 114% growth in producing agency branch locations and 79% growth in quote volumes.
quotes: A decline in the business of the Reciprocal almost certainly could have as a consequence a decline in the total premiums paid and a correspondingly adverse effect on the amount of the management fees received by our Insurance Services segment.
Top-of-funnel expansion continued, with Q3 2026 producing agency branch locations rising 114% from Q3 2025 and quote volumes rising 79% from Q3 2025.

business_model.claim: Porch's SaaS relationships with approximately 18 thousand companies provide early visibility into approximately 90% of U.S. homebuyers and homes before a move, enabling cross-selling of insurance, warranties, and moving services.
quotes: Beyond insurance, Porch is a leader in the home software-as-a-service (“SaaS”) space, serving approximately 18 thousand companies across industries essential to the home-buying process—home inspectors, title companies, mortgage providers, and more.

Our deep relationships and proprietary data give us unique visibility into approximately 90% of U.S. homebuyers and approximately 90% of U.S. homes, enabling superior risk assessment and competitive pricing.
We know when homebuyers are moving approximately six weeks before they move due to our unique early insight.

business_model.claim: Software & Data and consolidated revenue also respond to SaaS pricing actions (such as Rynoh's 20% price increase in Q1 2025), new Home Factors data monetization, and the share of insurance premiums retained by Porch's captive reinsurer rather than ceded externally.
quotes: In Software and Data, Rynoh implemented a 20% price increase in the first quarter, in line with strategic pricing goals.
We intend to add new categories of Home Factors, our property insights product, each quarter and further monetize Home Factors with third parties.
In 2025, our captive reinsurer retained a higher proportion of premiums than in the prior year.

business_model.claim: Consolidated cost of revenue was 119,568 (table in thousands) in the 9 months ended Sep. 30, 2026 versus 113,854 (table in thousands) in the prior-year period, and 142,424 (table in thousands) in 2025, driven primarily by claims experience, seasonal catastrophe weather, and repair-cost inflation.
quotes: The decrease was primarily the result of strong underwriting at the Reciprocal and fewer catastrophic weather events impacting the Reciprocal, which limited the number of claims.

Claims costs may be adversely affected by increases in costs of home repair as a result of inflated material costs, supply chain shortages, increases in labor costs, and demand surge during catastrophic events.
Property insurance claims fluctuate with seasonal weather; the highest exposure to catastrophic weather for the Reciprocal has historically occurred in the first half of the year.

business_model.claim: Reinsurance costs and retention terms are a central risk-transfer driver, with third-party excess-of-loss catastrophe coverage starting at $25.0 million per occurrence up to $410.0 million and 7.5% third-party quota share reducing effective Reciprocal retention to $23.1 million per occurrence.
quotes: As of April 1, 2025, coverage for excess of loss catastrophe reinsurance starts at $25.0 million per occurrence up to a loss of $410.0 million.

Additionally, the third-party quota share reinsurance contracts start immediately at 7.5% of property and casualty (“P&C”) losses, which includes catastrophe events, bringing the effective retention for the Reciprocal from $25.0 million per occurrence to $23.1 million per occurrence.

The availability of reinsurance and its price are generally determined in the reinsurance market by conditions beyond our control and can be negatively impacted by such severe weather events and the effects of climate change, including, tornado and hail events, hurricanes, extensive wildfires, drought, flooding and other catastrophes, and the frequency of such events, as well as the impacts of future global pandemics and other health crises, may harm the insurance business we manage and operate.

business_model.claim: Porch and the Reciprocal agreed to acquire Allied Trust's insurance carrier and managing general agency across Louisiana, Texas, South Carolina, and North Carolina, which is expected to operate under Porch's existing reciprocal and fee-based service structure if closed.
quotes: Allied Trust is a regional insurance carrier operating in Louisiana, Texas, South Carolina and North Carolina.
Following closing, Allied Trust is expected to operate under the same structure as Porch Group’s existing insurance business.
The Reciprocal will own the insurance carrier, collect premiums and pay claims, commissions, reinsurance costs and fees to Porch Group for operating services.

Our ability to access, collect and use personal information and property data provided by these parties may be adversely affected by federal and state laws and regulations that make it burdensome for us to collect or use personal information and property data.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.

In addition, our failure to respond to rapid and frequent changes in the pricing and operating dynamics of marketing channels, as well as changing policies and guidelines applicable to digital advertising, which may unilaterally be updated by search engines without advance notice, could adversely affect our digital marketing efforts and free search engine traffic.

We may not be able to consistently replicate favorable results with the use of Home Factors in underwriting for carriers other than HOA and the Reciprocal, which may be due to carrier location, modeling capabilities, or business goals of other carriers, and we may also face risks with regulators impacting our ability to use Home Factors.

quotes: Regulatory factors could, and a sustained decline in the price of our common stock would, negatively impact the Reciprocal’s statutory surplus, which may require it to raise additional funds to enable the Reciprocal to adhere to regulatory requirements and maintain its financial stability rating.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Part II Item 1A.

Integration may take longer, cost more, or prove more complex than we expect, and may result in the loss of key employees, agents, or policyholders of the acquired businesses and the diversion of management’s attention from our existing operations.

If personal, confidential, or sensitive user information or property data that we maintain and store is breached or otherwise accessed by unauthorized persons, it may be costly to mitigate, and our reputation could be harmed.
